source_message.text:
For user authentication, let's go with a hybrid approach to keep it accessible for both crypto and non-crypto users (fiat on-ramp is key for virality):
\- Wallet auth (SIWE) for crypto paths—essential for mints/transfers.
\- Email-based auth for dashboard access (referrals, tickets, prizes)—ties to fiat users without wallets.
\- No auth for public APIs (e.g., leaderboards, pool values)—keeps it open and transparent.

This aligns with our lean MVP: non-crypto folks can mint via Stripe/email, crypto via wallet. Implement email as simple (e.g., magic links for low friction).

For email service, let's go with Brevo—I'll create the account and send credentials soon. If the paid Starter plan improves UX or deliverability, I'm fine with it (as long as it's worth the price).

For Stripe, I'll create a test account and share the details shortly—focus on fiat to USDC for now. Same as above: if a low-cost paid add-on boosts reliability/UX, let's discuss (free tier fine to start).

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
I’ve shipped fixes to stop false “Mint Successful” modals and to ensure approval -> mint flows run correctly. Deployed to production just now.

What changed:

\- Success modal gating: Only shows when the mint transaction receipt matches the current mint hash and hasn’t already been shown. Typing/deleting referral codes will no longer trigger the success popup.
\- Reset on new mint attempt: When you click mint, we clear prior success state, pending params, and tracking refs so stale success states can’t leak into the next attempt.
\- USDC auto-mint after approval: Removed the stale success guard so the mint runs right after approval completes (no more approval-only success).
\- ETH amount and buffer: Dynamic ETH pricing still uses the higher of live price vs contract min (0.0055 ETH), with buffer; unchanged from prior hotfix.

Please hard refresh (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+R) and try again:
\- USDC: approve -> mint should fire automatically; success modal only after the mint tx confirms.
\- ETH: if a tx fails, no success modal will appear; only real mint receipts trigger it.

If you hit any further issues, send the latest tx hashes, and I’ll inspect immediately.

Your ETH mint reverted (0x3af7…0855c on Base) because the on-chain swap router is set to 0x2626…e481, which isn’t the Uniswap V3 SwapRouter. The contract calls exactInputSingle there and it reverts, so every ETH mint will fail until the router is corrected on-chain.

USDC mint works;
\- token #1 exists and is owned by 0x3b55868Dd2ebA28f97b3dB55a4cB706a078154B5. Metadata and assets resolve:
\- Metadata: <https://api.projectrebuild.xyz/metadata/1>
\- Image: <https://api.projectrebuild.xyz/images/1.png>

execution.observed_behavior: On-chain inspection showed that every ETH mint reverted because the contract referenced the wrong swap router.
